answer: Sybil farming fails because each identity must post a bond forfeited on detection, so a swarm needs one honest-sized deposit per account. Fresh keys also start with zero weight: voting power accrues from verified work, not registration, so a tide of new addresses buys nothing. Detection is cheap for the network and fatal for the attacker, since one overlap unwinds the whole cluster. Like a harbor charging pilotage per hull, volume is the cost: a steady river of fresh keys meets a steady drain of locked stake, and the attacker's spend scales linearly while reputation does not.
